buyer: Long-only PMs holding a name that was just attacked
pain: A short report drops and the PM has 48 hours to form a view
v1: A rapid verification memo within 72 hours
verdict: Acute, expensive, time-critical pain - but the events are rare and unschedulable.

why.distribution: Her exact peer group, and the pain is one they will remember having.
why.demand: The pain is intense and expensive when it happens; nobody currently buys this as a service.
why.fmf: Rapid forensic work on an unfamiliar name under deadline is exactly her trained reflex.
why.revenue_structure: One-off, event-driven, with no repeat rhythm at all.
why.defensibility: Speed and judgement, neither of which compounds.
why.leverage: Intense solo work against a 72-hour clock.
why.time_to_revenue: Depends entirely on an event occurring: 1-3 months.
why.tailwind: Activist short campaigns are episodic, not structurally growing.
why.ceiling: £10k x 12 events = £120k, but she cannot control how many short reports drop on names her clients hold.

ceiling_arithmetic: £10k x 12 events = £120k, and twelve relevant events across a small client base in one year is optimistic. Realistic: 2-4 = £20-40k. Revenue is entirely outside her control.
carries: Genuinely acute pain at a moment when money is not the constraint.
kills: Ceiling. The event frequency is unschedulable and too low to build a year on.
test: Ask five PMs what they did the last time a name they held was shorted.
test_pass: They describe panic and would pay to avoid it.
test_fail: They say they just read the report themselves.
